newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks edge over 700-point barrier.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks edge over 700-point barrier.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed above the psychological 700-point barrier on Tuesday on active locally-led buying in some blue chips and secondaries, brokers said.

They said the composite index edged up on sustained high interest in several units of the Lippo Group in particular, combined with rises in some blue chip stocks including Bank Negara Indonesia and Citra Marga.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.94 points, or 0.56 percent, to close at 701.31 points. Gainers led losers by 71 to 58, with 59 counters unchanged.

A broker with a European securities house said he expected some small and medium-sized stocks would become a market focus on Wednesday, with local investors likely to continue dominating overall trade.
"On the foreign side, I don't see enough fundamental reasons for active buying of blue chips," he said, referring to the relatively small foreign activity in the market on Tuesday.
Lippo Securities, Multipolar, Lippo Bank and Lippo Karawaci of the Lippo Group were actively traded, brokers said.
Lippo Securities was the most active stock, rising 250 rupiah to 3,550 rupiah on a volume 32.9 million shares.

Brokers said it was linked to a company plan for a stock split from a nominal value of 1,000 rupiah to 500 rupiah by March 3. Tuesday was the last day before the stock exchange suspended trading in Lippo Securities until Friday, February 28.
Multipolar rose 325 rupiah to 2,800 rupiah on 17.3 million shares on both speculative and fresh buying, brokers said.

Brokers said the stock had got a boost from recent news that Hari Darmawan, founder of retailer Matahari, planned to buy a stake in Multipolar after the company won shareholder approval to take a 50.1 percent controlling interest in Matahari.
Banking stocks Bank International Indonesia (BII) and Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) were actively traded on fresh buying, brokers said.
BII rose 75 rupiah to 2,025 rupiah on a turnover of 13.1 million shares, while BNI traded unchanged at 1,700 rupiah on 10 million shares.
Brokers said the two banks were the favourite stocks in the sector where active buying of one counter can spark interest in other banking stock.
Polyester maker PT Indorama Synthetics was also active after it announced net profit of 122 billion rupiah in 1996 against 120 billion rupiah in 1995.
Indorama also said it expected to make a net profit of 148 billion rupiah with total sales of 934 billion rupiah in 1997.
It rose 125 rupiah to 2,125 rupiah on a volume of one million shares. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
